competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency explicitly requires ordering 'from smallest to largest, and vice versa,' but every one of the 6 samples (seeds 42-46, 50) uses only the instruction 'Arrange these numbers from smallest to largest' -- the largest-to-smallest direction never appears in this node's own packet.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 'vice versa' sub-case named in the competency text is 0 for 6: not one of seeds 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, or 50 asks the student to order from largest to smallest, even though set sizes vary from 3 to 5 numbers.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sets of 3-5 two-digit numbers, e.g. '33, 38, 37, 26, 24' in seed 44, fit grade 2 quarter 1 ordering demand without excess cognitive load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: List size genuinely varies (3 numbers in seed 42, 5 numbers in seed 44) and formatter varies (ordering vs sort_order in seed 50), but the ordering direction never varies across any sample.

competency_alignment.rationale: Where tested, correctly ordering '28, 36, 41, 29, 32' into '28, 29, 32, 36, 41' (seed 50) directly targets this competency's smallest-to-largest ordering skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency ceiling is 1000, but the highest number across all 6 samples is 62 (seed 43); every sample stays two-digit, with nothing approaching the hundreds.
